claim: A disputed assessment must generally first be appealed to the county board of equalization where the property is located or it becomes final.

claim: The county board of equalization generally convenes June 1 (Shelby County May 1).
Appeals to the State Board of Equalization from a county board must be filed by August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the date notice of the county board action was sent, whichever is later.
cite: Appealing to the State Board of Equalization (Value Appeals)

claim: An SBOE appeal is first heard by an Administrative Judge, who issues an Initial Decision and Order within 90 days of the hearing.
Judicial review of a final SBOE action requires a petition in chancery court within 60 days from when the order becomes final.
The appellant must show by a preponderance of the evidence the correct assessment; sales of comparable properties are generally the best evidence for residential property.
Taxpayers must pay at least the undisputed portion of taxes before the delinquency date to avoid penalties and interest while an appeal is pending.
Assessment ratios: residential real property 25%, farm real property 25%, commercial and industrial real property 40%, public utility property 55%, business personal property 30%.

Tennessee's Property Tax Relief program reimburses part or all of paid property taxes for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled veteran homeowners or surviving spouses; it is not an exemption and the owner still receives and pays the tax bill.
Tax relief applies only to the primary residence, one property per tax year.
The program began in 1973 following the 1972 constitutional amendment.

A local-option property tax freeze for homeowners 65 or older exists in participating counties/cities; taxes on the principal residence are frozen at a base amount, subject to annual application and a county income limit.
Tax Relief and Tax Freeze application deadlines are 35 days past the local property tax delinquency date.

Within one year from the order confirming a delinquent tax sale, any person with a legal or equitable interest may redeem by paying the court clerk the taxes, interest, penalties, costs and court-ordered charges plus 10% per annum interest on the entire purchase price from the date of sale.
On the purchaser's motion the redeeming person may also have to pay property taxes and money the purchaser spent to preserve the property during redemption.
Delinquent tax sales are conducted through the court (clerk and master or court clerk) and proceeds pay taxes first.
Property tax delinquency date for the prior year's taxes is March 1; February 28 is the last day to pay without interest.
